groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if the NVMe device(s) in this vSAN cluster is/are compatible with the vSAN configuration type as per vSAN VCG (VMware Compatibility Guide).

groupTests.testName: Controller disk group mode is VMware certified
groupTests.testDescription: Checks if the vSAN disk group type (All-Flash or Hybrid) is certified for the used SCSI controller in the VMware Compatibility Guide. Only the controller which is on the vSAN HCL and certified for the current release of ESXi will be tested and shown in the result.

groupTests.riskIfNotFix: adherence to the vmware compatibility guide (vcg)/hardware compatibility guide (hcl) is critically important to the stability of vsan environments. using a noncompliant controller/disk or incorrect controller configuration for vsan (including the driver, firmware, disk mode, etc) puts the user data at risk, and could lead to severe issues of data unavailability over time.

groupTests.testDescription: Checks the status of the vSAN performance service. Warning from this check can be remediated by enabling vSAN performance service following VMware vSAN administration guide.
groupTests.testShortDescription: VMware recommends that all deployments of vSAN have the vSAN performance service enabled. It provides access to real time and historic performance data of vSAN.
groupTests.riskIfNotFix: there will be no vsan performance data collected from both real-time and historical views which may make it impossible for troubleshooting any vsan performance-related issues.

groupTests.testDescription:
vSAN Support Insight is a platform intended to assist vSAN users in maintaining a reliable and consistent computing, storage and network environment.
When you choose to participate in "vCenter Customer Experience Improvement Program" (CEIP), VMware will collect technical information about use of products and services in the environment on a regular cadence. This enables VMware to provide improved customer support experience with comprehensive online health checks and performance diagnostics. The collected information does not personally identify customers.
In case a customer do not wish to participate in CEIP, they can choose to enable "vSAN Online Notifications" and build the network connectivity with VMware's Analytics Cloud. This will enable vSAN Health Notifications for software and hardware issues. When you opt for vSAN Online Notifications, VMware will not collect any data from the VMware VMware vCenter.
groupTests.testShortDescription: vSAN Support Insight Health Check.

values: Not joined the Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP). Join CEIP to get better support.
Enabled. Cluster can receive vSAN notifications from VMware cloud.

groupTests.testDescription: To ensure proper functionality, all vSAN hosts must be able to communicate over both multicast and unicast. If they cannot, a vSAN cluster will split into multiple partitions, i.e. sub-groups of hosts that can communicate, but not to other sub-groups. When that happens, vSAN objects might become unavailable until the network misconfiguration is resolved.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if the vSAN cluster is partitioned due to a network issue.

groupTests.testName: All hosts have a vSAN vmknic configured
groupTests.testDescription: In order to participate in a vSAN cluster, and form a single group of fully connected hosts, each host in a vSAN cluster must have a vmknic (VMkernel network interface or VMkernel adapter) configured for vSAN traffic.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if all the hosts in the vSAN cluster have a configured vmknic with vSAN traffic enabled.

testDetails.label: Hosts with no vSAN vmknic present

groupTests.testDescription: This check refers to situations where VC lists the host as connected, but API calls from VC to the host are failing. This should be extremely rare, but in case it happens it leads to similar issues as the Host disconnected from VC situation.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if API calls from VC to a host are failing while the host is in connected state.

groupTests.testDescription: This check refers to whether VC has an active connection to all hosts in the cluster. If any host is disconnected from VC (or not responding) it could cause operational issues. If VC is not connected to the host, its state is unknown to VC. The host may be up, and may be participating in the vSAN cluster, serving data, and playing a critical role in the storage functions of the cluster. Or the host may be down and unavailable. VC and hence the vSAN Health check cannot fully assess the situation as long the host is disconnected. If the host is participating in the vSAN cluster it will show up in the Unexpected vSAN cluster member check as unexpected, as its UUID cannot be determined, so the health check cannot conclusively tell if the host it is seeing in the vSAN cluster is the disconnected one or not. In addition, other health checks, like vSAN connectivity checks or disk health checks will not be able to take the disconnected host into account.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if VC has an active connection to all hosts in the cluster.

groupTests.testDescription: Performs a ping test with small packet size from each host to all other hosts. If this check fails, there is a basic issue with network connectivity. Check vmknic, uplink, VLAN, physical switch and associated settings. If this check passes, basic unicast connectivity is working properly.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Performs a ping test with small packet size from each host to all other hosts.

groupTests.testName: vSAN: MTU check (ping with large packet size)
groupTests.testDescription: Performs a ping test with large packet size from each host to all other hosts. If this check fails while the basic connectivity check passes, there is an issue with MTU settings.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Performs a ping test with large packet size from each host to all other hosts.

groupTests.testDescription: Performs a ping test with small packet size between all VMkernel adapters with vMotion traffic enabled.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Performs a ping test with small packet size between all VMkernel adapters with vMotion traffic enabled.

groupTests.testName: vMotion: MTU check (ping with large packet size)
groupTests.testDescription: Performs a ping test with large packet size between all VMKernel adapters with vMotion traffic enabled.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Performs a ping test with large packet size between all VMKernel adapters with vMotion traffic enabled.

groupTests.testDescription: Performs a network latency check of vSAN hosts. The network configuration guidance of normal cluster requires RTT less than 1ms. To allow for temporary fluctuations, this health check reports warnings based on a conservative threshold of 5ms. If this check fails, please check vmknic, uplink, VLAN, physical switch and associated settings to locate the network issue. NOTE: This check will be skipped if the pair of hosts failed connectivity check.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Performs a network latency check of vSAN hosts. It requires <1ms RTT. To allow for temporary fluctuations, this health check reports warnings based on a conservative threshold of 5ms. NOTE: This check will be skipped if the pair of hosts failed connectivity check.

groupTests.testDescription: Check if there are duplicate IP addresses configured for vmknic interfaces. Any services that rely on the misconfigured interface might be affected by IP network connectivity issues.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Check if there are duplicate IP addresses configured for vmknic interfaces. Any services that rely on the misconfigured interface might be affected by IP network connectivity issues.

groupTests.testDescription: Check if TSO (TCP Segmentation Offload) is enabled for pNIC. TSO on the transmission path of physical network adapters improves the performance of ESXi hosts by reducing the overhead of the CPU for TCP/IP network operations. When TSO is enabled, the network adapter divides larger data chunks into TCP segments instead of the CPU.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Check if TSO (TCP Segmentation Offload) is enabled for pNIC. TSO on the transmission path of physical network adapters improves the performance of ESXi hosts by reducing the overhead of the CPU for TCP/IP network operations. When TSO is enabled, the network adapter divides larger data chunks into TCP segments instead of the CPU.

groupTests.testDescription: Check if LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) is working properly. LACP is a standards-based method to control the bundling of several physical network links together to form a logical channel for increased bandwidth and redundancy purposes.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Check if LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) is working properly. LACP is a standards-based method to control the bundling of several physical network links together to form a logical channel for increased bandwidth and redundancy purposes.

groupTests.testDescription: Checks the physical disk operation health for vSAN disk for all hosts in the vSAN cluster. For vSAN disk if this check fails, the disk cannot be used by vSAN anymore with the possible reasons like issue in reading the disk metadata or the vSAN software issue preventing it to use this disk.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the operation health of the physical disks for all hosts in the vSAN cluster.

groupTests.testDescription: There are critical drive events reported from storage vendor with potential drive operation risk. Follow the vendor message for further troubleshooting and remediation.
groupTests.testShortDescription: There are critical drive events reported from storage vendor with potential drive operation risk. Follow the vendor message for further troubleshooting and remediation.

groupTests.testDescription: If this health status not green/OK, vSAN is still using the disk, but it is in a state of (possibly severely) reduced performance, manifesting in low throughput/IOPS and high latencies for vSAN objects using this disk.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks whether vSAN is using the disk with reduced performance.

groupTests.testDescription: Checks if the number of components on the physical disk reaches the maximum limit.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the component limits on each physical disk.

groupTests.testDescription: This check will fail if vSAN has encountered an issue with the integrity of the metadata of a component in this disk. This could be due to faulty drives, faulty controller or a misbehaving device driver, but could also originate from a problem in the vSAN software. The best course of action is to engage VMware Support.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks whether vSAN has encountered an integrity issue of the metadata of a component on this disk.

groupTests.testDescription: This check will fail if vSAN is running low on vital memory pools needed for the correct operation of physical disks. Even under high load, this should not happen. If it does happen, VMware Support should be contacted. Likely the disk will also report bad congestion health, which will in turn lead to performance issues.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if vSAN is running low on vital memory pools, needed for the correct operation of physical disks.

groupTests.testDescription: This check will fail if vSAN is running low on a vital memory pool needed for the operation of physical disks. Even under high load, this should not happen. If it does happen, VMware Support should be contacted. Likely the disk will also report bad congestion health, which will in turn lead to performance issues.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if vSAN is running low on the vital memory pool, needed for the operation of physical disks.

groupTests.testDescription: If this check fails for a specific disk, it indicates that this disk is low on free disk space. For clusters with vSAN space efficiency feature enabled (deduplication and compression, or compression-only), the logical used space will be checked as well. The disk logical space indicates the space required before applying vSAN space efficiency, while the physical space indicates the space used after applying vSAN space efficiency. This health check is only applicable to capacity tier devices, not to the cache tier devices.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the free space on physical disks in the vSAN cluster.

groupTests.testDescription: Checks whether the vSAN in-use disk matches the licensed disk information.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks whether the vSAN in-use disk matches the licensed disk information.

groupTests.testDescription: Provides a cluster wide overview by summarizing all objects in the cluster, grouping them in fine grained categories of object health.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the health status of all vSAN objects.

actionDescription.message: Repairs the absent or degraded vSAN objects immediately.
Purges all inaccessible VM swap objects in the vSAN cluster

groupTests.testDescription: Provides a cluster wide overview of all objects that need change in object format. The object format change may involve physical on-disk re-layout of objects which can cause data movement in the cluster. Object count indicates the number of objects in old format and not in the process of format change. Those objects might not be able to use some of the new features. Please check Resyncing Objects view for detailed format change progress.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if any vSAN objects need format change.

actionDescription.message: Changes the object format by relaying out the objects.

groupTests.testName: Time is synchronized across hosts and VC
groupTests.testDescription: Checks time difference among VC and hosts. Any difference larger than 60 seconds will lead this check to fail. If the check fails, it is recommended that you check the NTP server configuration.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks that time of hosts and VC are synchronized within 1 minute.

groupTests.testDescription: vSAN has a number of advanced config options that can be used for tuning or to address special requirements of particular deployments. Usually such settings get changed under the guidance of VMware Support, using a VMware KB article procedure. These advanced config options are set per host, which makes it easy to create inconsistent configurations across a cluster. This check ensures that critical vSAN advanced config options have the same value or default value across all hosts in a given cluster.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if all of the hosts in a vSAN cluster have consistent non-default advanced configuration options. The advanced configuration with default value will be skipped and not shown in the result.

groupTests.testDescription: Check liveness of several critical host daemons on all of the vSAN hosts. NOTE: CLOMD status won't be checked on witness node. EPD, OSFSD and cmmdsTimemachined status won't be checked on witness and metadata node. VBOSSD status will be checked if VCF Native Object Store service is enabled, and it won't be checked on witness and metadata node.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks critical vSAN daemons liveness

groupTests.testDescription: This check helps a user monitor the balance state among disks. By default "Automatic Rebalance" is disabled, status of this health check turns yellow if the imbalance exceeds a system-determined threshold. When 'Automatic Rebalance' is enabled, vSAN automatically rebalances to keep the status always green. Rebalance can wait up to 30 minutes to start, giving time to high priority tasks like EMM, repair, etc. to use the resources before rebalancing.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the vSAN disk balance status on all hosts.

groupTests.testDescription: Checks if the resync operations are throttled on any hosts. Shows a warning when resync bandwidth limit is configured and shows an error when the value is less than 20 MBps. Please clear the limit, unless you need it for particular cases like significant resync traffic causing high VM latencies. Setting this limit may make resync-based operations like policy change or maintenance mode slower.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if the resync operations are throttled on any hosts.

groupTests.testDescription: If this check fails, it shows yellow to warn user that vSAN Direct disks are not homogeneously claimed among hosts. In which uneven distribution of capacity can lead to some of the pods remaining in pending state forever.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if all hosts in cluster claimed vSAN Direct disks with same capacity, disk mode and number.

groupTests.testDescription: During normal operation, VMware vCenter state is regarded as source of truth, and ESXi hosts are automatically updated with the latest host membership list. When VMware vCenter is replaced or recovered from backup, the host membership list in VMware vCenter may be out of sync. This health check detects such cases, and alerts if VMware vCenter state was not pushed to ESXi due to VMware vCenter being out of sync. In such cases, first fully restore the membership list in VMware vCenter, and then perform 'Update ESXi configuration' action if required.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if VMware vCenter state is pushed to ESXi, and the host membership is not out of sync.

testDetails.label: Hosts that are out of sync

actionDescription.message: Update ESXi configuration which is out of sync with current VMware vCenter.

groupTests.testDescription: There are inconsistent configuration (like deduplication, compression, encryption) setup on hosts or disks with the cluster.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if the hosts and disks have a consistent configuration with the cluster.

actionDescription.message: Remediate hosts and disks which have inconsistent configurations (e.g. dedup/compression, encryption) with the cluster.

groupTests.testName: vSphere cluster members match vSAN cluster members
groupTests.testDescription: Checks that vSphere cluster members match vSAN cluster members
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks that vSphere cluster members match vSAN cluster members

groupTests.testDescription: Once a vSAN cluster starts using a new on-disk format version (after software upgrade), the cluster becomes incompatible with hosts of older software version that do not support the new on-disk format. If such an older host version is introduced in the cluster, this host is either in a network partition or can only see/access a very limited set of data in the cluster. Such configurations are unsupported and an immediate software upgrade or removal of the older host version are advised.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the software version compatibility of all in-use hosts.

groupTests.testDescription: vSAN cluster expected format version is 21, which is the highest supported format version by any host in the cluster. For disk with format version lower than expected version, vSAN on-disk format upgrade is recommended, to support latest vSAN features.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks format version of all in-use vSAN disks, expected format version is 21.

columns.label: Number of disks with older format

actionDescription.message: Performing a vSAN on-disk format upgrade, which is a long running operation. It will upgrade one disk group at a time, and for each disk group it will evacuate all data stored on that disk group, remove the old vSAN format and re-add the disk group to vSAN with the new format.

groupTests.testDescription: Checks if all of the hosts in a vSAN cluster have consistent vSAN extended configurations. For host with inconsistent extended configurations, vSAN cluster remediation is recommended, for host doesn't support any extended configuration, ESXi software upgrade is needed; And to make cluster scalability configuration take effect, host reboot could be required.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks if all of the hosts in a vSAN cluster have consistent vSAN extended configurations.

actionDescription.message: Remediate hosts and disks which have inconsistent configurations (e.g. dedup/compression, encryption) with the cluster.

groupTests.testDescription: Check if the usage of vSAN datastore capacity and vSAN managed datastore of the cluster is beyond the thresholds. If there is not enough free space, the deployment of new workload may fail or component rebuild operations may not be allowed. The running workload may have pending issues.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks for free capacity tier disk space across the entire cluster

groupTests.testDescription: Checks for the component utilization for the entire cluster and each host and show warning or error if the utilization exceeds than 80% or 90% in any of host. Since each vSAN object is composed of a set of components, determined by capabilities that are in use in the VM Storage Policy, the deployment of new virtual machines may fail, nor a rebuild operations can be allowed if the component limit has been reached, and you have to either add more host or delete some of vSAN objects. However, if the component is full in witness node, you have to replace it with bigger capacity.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the component utilization for the whole cluster and each host in the vSAN cluster

groupTests.testName: What if the most consumed host fails
groupTests.testDescription: This health check simulates the failure of the host with most resources consumed and shows the cluster resource consumption then. First, the resources on that host would be no longer available. Second, vSAN will attempt to re-protect all objects that were now running with reduced redundancy. Re-protection of all objects is impossible if utilization is more than 100%.
groupTests.testShortDescription: Checks the vSAN component limits, disk space and RC reservations assuming one host failure.
